title: The Loving
hookLine: one of God's names in the Quran: the Loving
carry: love that is warm and shows

cards: The Quran calls God by name after name: the Merciful, the Wise, the Hearing, the Seeing.

In Muslim practice they're recited and reflected on, and some parents give them to their children, joined to the word Abd, servant: Abd al-Rahman, servant of the Merciful. One of the names can catch a listener off guard.
It isn't power, or knowledge, or judgment. It's warmth. Al-Wadud.

teach.b: First, the word. Tradition links al-Wadud to wudd, an Arabic word for affection: not a distant goodwill, but love that is warm and shows.

Elsewhere the Quran says that for those who believe and do good, the Merciful will appoint love, using that same word. Love, in this picture, is something God gives and also places between people. Second, the neighbors.
The name appears in the chapter called al-Buruj, the Constellations, and Pickthall translates it: "And He is the Forgiving, the Loving."
Some readers notice the order: forgiveness first, then a love still there afterward, not a pardon given at arm's length. Third, the setting, which is the surprise.

That chapter opens with a terrible story, the people of the ditch, a fire, and believers tormented only because they believed. A few verses later, the punishment it warns of is for those who persecute and "repent not."
Some commentators point to those words: even for people that cruel, a door is described as still open. Right after comes the name: the Forgiving, the Loving.
In another chapter the prophet Shuayb tells his people to ask pardon and turn back, and says, "Lo! my Lord is Merciful, Loving." Again, love beside mercy. Fourth, a Sufi voice.

People tell a story about Rabia of Basra, an early woman mystic, carrying a torch and a bucket of water through the streets: to burn paradise and put out hell, she said, so that God would be loved for God alone.
It's a story told, not a text, but it points at the same name.

how: Muslims call on God by His names in prayer and remembrance, and some reflect on one name at a time, such as al-Wadud, the Loving, and try to show something of it in how they treat others.

o: the Forgiving, the name for God's pardon
God's name in the Quran for warm, loving affection
the Merciful, the name in Abd al-Rahman

games.q: inside the name — tap the pairs.

s: in al-Buruj, the Loving stands next to the Forgiving
"And He is the Forgiving, the Loving."
the story of Rabia's torch and bucket is a verse of the Quran
it's a story people tell about her, not a text.
the warning in al-Buruj leaves no mention of repenting
it is for those who persecute and "repent not."

games.q: a chapter of the Quran tells of the people of the ditch, who tormented believers beside a fire. a few verses later, which names of God follow?
games.why: the Forgiving, the Loving. after a story of cruelty, the chapter names forgiveness and warm love.

practice: Ask yourself who could use a loving word today, maybe someone you've had to forgive, or who has had to forgive you, and picture them.
Find one warm word, or a few, that you could actually say: I'm glad you called, thank you for waiting for me, it's good to see you.
Let it be simple and true, and if you pray, you can call on God as al-Wadud, the Loving, in your own way.

wordCard.voice: Al-Wadud. The Loving: one of God's names in the Quran, love that is warm and shows, set right beside the Forgiving. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Loving, one of God's names in the Quran, linked by tradition to wudd, affection.

carryVoice: Your line: love that is warm and shows. The Forgiving, and then the Loving. See you tomorrow.
